completed: H3 t2v FAIL SETTLED - and BOTH candidates in the previous handoff were wrong, each disproven for FREE before renting anything. (a) The MPI-501 drain-wait hole was never reached: the app's only server-side restart caller (routes/remoteModels.js:906) is gated on out.installed.length, and the app log for the failing run reads 'universal nodes: 7/7 already on volume' - the ONLY log line in the whole 07:13-07:44Z window. No restart fired. 2ad444a2 is a correct fix for a real hole but is not the fix for this. (b) 'start.sh:193's supervisor relaunching ComfyUI' does not exist - :193 is node-dedupe, ComfyManager._supervise calls os._exit(1) on unexpected death and start.sh ends in `exec uvicorn` with no respawn, so a crash takes the CONTAINER down.

The VRAM theory is dead too, on FABIO'S argument: i2v carries the same 24.55GB text encoder PLUS an image path so it cannot be cheaper, and it passes on the same Pod minutes after t2v fails. Do not re-open 'bigger card for H3's leg'.

THE RETRY PASSED - minimax-h3/t2v_ms, 153s, 1 out. Evidence merged: 35 PASS / 0 SKIP / 0 FAIL over 35 ops. A /remote/comfy/status poll ran alongside the whole run and showed an UNDISTURBED Pod (ready:true, comfyReady:true unbroken 11:25:07Z-11:28:10Z). NOTE: that evidence is now VOID for 1.4 because the engine is being bumped - see pending.

FOUND + FIXED the likely cause, in the RUNNER not the app: orphanReason guarded the QUEUE read against a failed fetch but NOT the history re-read, so `.catch(() => null)` collapsed 'could not read' into 'absent from history' - and absent-from-history is half of what declares an orphan. The op takes 153s; the FAIL was declared at 162s, i.e. at the completion boundary where that read is likeliest to fail. NOT PROVEN to be what bit us (the Pod is deleted and the run that would prove it is the one that passed) - it is a defect that can manufacture this exact verdict. tests/smoke-orphan-guard.test.cjs, 5 tests, mutation-verified, incl. a negative control proving a REAL absence still reports.

Also removed the runner's diagnostic claim 'only POST /wrapper/restart-comfy does that, a crash would have taken the Pod down' - it named a caller that provably did not fire, and that sentence is what sent the previous session hunting. The sound half (the wrapper mechanics) is kept as a comment; the conclusion is gone.

FOUND + FIXED a second runner defect, via Fabio's ComfyUI PR link: the frame budget NEVER REACHED H3. TITLE_RULES clamps Input_Frames, but H3 expresses length in SECONDS - Input_Duration (MpiInt) feeds MpiH3Length, 24fps on an n%17==5 grid. So minimax-h3/t2v_ms was smoking a 3-second ~73-frame video while every other op ran ONE frame, which is the plain reason H3 took 153s against 4-38s elsewhere, on every matrix run, on a rented GPU. Now clamps Input_Duration to 1 (~22 frames; the shipped r2va graph already bakes exactly 1, so it is proven-legal). Verified against BOTH real H3 graphs plus a self-check assertion.

NOTES AUDITED - mpi-kanban:claim-auditor over all 524 lines against v1.3.1..HEAD (593 commits): ~45 PROVEN, 1 FALSE, 4 OVERSTATED, 1 UNPROVABLE. Every finding re-verified by hand against git BEFORE any edit, which mattered: ONE FINDING WAS ITSELF WRONG (it claimed ltx-23 declares VideoHelperSuite and wanted the notes to say 'Wan 2.2 or LTX 2.3'; the two declarations are inside wan-22 at models.js:1106 and wan22-5b at :1454 - applying that fix would have PUT a false claim into a public changelog). Treat that agent as evidence, never truth.

NOTES CORRECTED: the FALSE one (Chroma's Control op DOES follow the source image - both Chroma cards declare imageSizedOps ['control','detail','upscale']; the Depth->Control rename left the line stale); the six progress bars restated as the TWO root causes they had (fa7f2dc1 sibling-billing on 2, be00aee7 orphan collection on 4); 'both Qwen models' -> 'Qwen' (there is exactly one); and UNRELEASED.md:176's 'nothing extra to download' corrected after verifying neither preview decoder carries engineAsset:true and syncModelInstalled resolves the FULL dep universe, so an existing H3/LTX owner really does land in partial state.

CUT on Fabio's call: the whole 'LTX video generation works again' bullet. It claimed every LTX generation had failed since the 1.3.0 release, but v1.3.0 AND v1.3.1 BOTH pinned ComfyUI v0.29.2 and the breaking change is in v0.30.0 - pinned only in this dev cycle. No released user ever had broken LTX. The bullet described a regression created and fixed inside the cycle, invisible to everyone.

The '2m15s instead of 4m15s' figure had no committed backing (turbo.md holds only the 2-second lightx2v measurement and a 5s table for the OTHER LoRA - the turbo LoRA was swapped mid-cycle, MPI-505 -> MPI-508). READ THAT FIRST - it is written to be executed in order and this list does not repeat it.

TRAP 1 - node_lock.json pins the FRONTEND as well as core, so THREE pins move, not one: comfyui-frontend-package 1.47.11 -> 1.48.7 and comfyui-workflow-templates 0.11.27 -> 0.11.34, both read from v0.31.0's own requirements.txt. The playbook's 'bump the pin in BOTH files' means node_lock + system_dependencies and never mentions these.

TRAP 2 - res_multistep changed RNG consumption (#15339: `if sigmas[i+1] > 0` -> `if sigma_up > 0`) and FOUR shipped graphs use it: chroma_t2i, chroma_hyper_t2i, minimax_h3_fl2va, minimax_h3_r2va. Where sigma_up==0 the old code still CALLED noise_sampler and multiplied by zero, advancing the RNG; the new code skips it, so the seed->image mapping can shift. UNVERIFIED - prove it at the LOCAL gate with the same seed on 0.30 vs 0.31 before writing or omitting a release note. If it shifts, that is an importantChanges line, because users with saved seeds get different pictures.

TWO Pod image builds this release, not one: the DEV image for the smoke, and then a MANDATORY STABLE rebuild at release. An engine bump makes the release-time rebuild compulsory - ship the app at 0.31 while the released image is still 0.30 and every remote user silently runs two different ComfyUI versions. Promotion is a clean rebuild at a real version, NEVER a dev tag renamed, so there is no const to promote. mpi-release's 'a dev-only Pod IMAGE tag needs no action' is explicitly untrue for an engine bump.

THE SMOKE EVIDENCE IS VOID and must be a FULL matrix, not --retry-failed: release-health-check.mjs:463 refuses a file produced against a different engine, so all 35 rows die with the pin move. It is cheaper than this morning though - H3 now clamps Input_Duration to 1 (~22 frames, was ~73) and the volume is warm at 327.3GB of 450GB.

ORDERING - RUN THE SMOKE LAST, AFTER FABIO'S NEW H3 VAE DEP LANDS. Told 2026-08-10 13:0x: a new, smaller, faster H3 VAE just shipped (H3 now ~27s, down from ~40s on 0.31 and ~70s on 0.30). Fabio is adding it in a PARALLEL SESSION as a dependency change and will continue this handoff when it is in. It is almost certainly what `Support int8_convrot VAE for MiniMax-H3` (kijai #15334) enables, so it REQUIRES 0.31 and belongs in 1.4 with the bump. THE TRAP: release:check gates the evidence on the ENGINE version but NOT on the dep set, so a matrix run BEFORE the VAE lands looks perfectly valid while describing a model that no longer exists - and the whole rented matrix is wasted. This is the same shape as the playbook's 'sync LAST' lesson about node_lock and python_deps being live working-tree state. Confirm the VAE dep is in the tree, then smoke.

The new VAE also needs a release-notes line and must be added to the claim-audit set - it is a user-facing speed claim, and the standing rule is NO SPECIFIC NUMBERS unless a committed artifact backs them (smoke-evidence.json or a docs/models/h3/ timing table). Fabio's 27s is a bench reading, not committed evidence.
